newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES SIGN IRABU TO FOUR-YEAR DEAL WORTH $13 MILLION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES SIGN IRABU TO FOUR-YEAR DEAL WORTH $13 MILLION.

text.p: The New York Yankees on Thursday finally signed Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu on a four-year contract believed to be worth about $13 million.

With the 27-year-old Irabu agreeing to terms, the Yankees will send the San Diego Padres $3 million in cash, outfielder Ruben Rivera and minor-league pitcher Rafael Medina. In addition to Irabu, New York will receive minor-leaguers Homer Bush, Gordon Amerson and a player to be named.

The deal was contingent upon the Yankees being able to sign Irabu to a contract by Saturday. Both Medina and Rivera are recovering from injuries, and Rivera is recovering from shoulder surgery from spring training.
Irabu is expected to pitch in the Yankees' minor-league system before joining the team.

"It'll be three or four weeks before he gets here," Yankees manager Joe Torre said Thursday. "I think I'm going to wait a couple of weeks to see what we need at the time. I think the most important thing is what he's able to do."
The Padres owned the rights to the bulky 260-pound (117.9 kg) Irabu as a result of their working agreement with the pitcher's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.
But Irabu was steadfast in his desire to pitch only for the Yankees and claimed he was prepared to sit out the entire season if he was not traded to New York.

Irabu was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season. He was 38-27 in the last three seasons. In nine years with the Lotte Orions and the Marines he was 59-59 with a 3.41 ERA and 1,111 strikeouts in 1,101.2 innings.

Irabu would become the fourth Japanese player in the major leagues, joining three other pitchers -- Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shigetoshi Hasegawa of the Anaheim Angels and Takashi Kashiwada of the New York Mets.
It is believed Irabu has received the biggest contract ever for a player who has never played in the major leagues.
The expansion Tampa Bay Devil Rays gave pitcher Matt White a $10.2 million deal last November.
Irabu's soon-to-be teammates with the Yankees do not appear to be bothered with the contract.

"I don't care, to be honest with you," said shortstop Derek Jeter. "If he's that good, give him the money. They say he's the Nolan Ryan of Japan, so if he's Nolan Ryan, he's going to help. We'll see when he gets here."
